series.label: Annualised funding by asset (latest hourly print × 8760)

notes: Hedge is 1:1 in token quantity (spot qty = perp qty), so dollar delta is zero up to szDecimals rounding and fee/funding flows.
Close triggers: latest funding ≤ 0 (hourly), price ≥ 0.8 × liquidation price (15 min in prod), hedge drift > 5% (5 min), orphaned leg repair.

Costs: taker 3.5 bps per perp leg, 4 bps spot, 5 bps realised slippage per leg, 5 bps spot–perp basis crossed per open and per close; 50 bps limit-price tolerance is used for sizing only. 8% of opens leave one leg part-filled for an hour, which is what trips the drift / orphaned-leg checks in production too.
Data: 90 days of Hyperliquid hourly funding and Binance 1h spot (HYPE from Hyperliquid candles), fetched 2026-10-23 and bundled in data/; `fetch_data.py` refreshes them.

tables.title: Reference: production PT-sENA backtest (real data, Feb–Apr 2026)
tables.md:
Numbers from the deployed PT-sENA backtest page I built at Lucidly (ENA fell ~25%, 88-day hold, $100k, 15% HL reserve, 1x):

| item | value |
|---|---|
| Net PnL | +$1.6k (+1.65%), 6.83% annualised |
| Funding earned | $84.86 |
| Fees | −$72.35 (Pendle $33.37, HL $38.98) |
| Max drawdown | −$885 (−0.89%) |
| PT deployed / short notional | $41.7k (311,070 PT) / $43.3k @ $0.1393 |
| Liquidation price | $0.3172 (128% above entry); worst margin health 4,251% |
| PT leg / short leg at maturity | −$9.4k / +$11.0k |
| Deployment | 5 chunks × max $20k, 1-hour spacing (HL book depth) |
| What-if reserve in stablecoin at 4% | +1.79% / 7.43% APY vs 4.00% pure stablecoin |

Arithmetic reconciles: −9.4k + 11.0k + 84.86 − 72.35 ≈ +1.6k; 1.65% × 365/88 ≈ 6.84%; implied PT entry $0.134 = 3.8% discount to spot.

notes: The PT leg has less than one token of delta before maturity (it trades at a discount), while the hedge is fixed at 1.0 per PT, so the book is net short early and the drift converges to zero at maturity — visible in the drift series.
This scenario is a model path (terminal −25% pinned) so the engine always builds; the reference table is the real-data result.

sections.heading: What this is
sections.body_md: A USDC vault on HyperEVM running a multi-asset cash-and-carry on Hyperliquid: buy the HyperCore spot token (USOL, UBTC, HYPE, UETH), sell the same token quantity in the perp at 3x, and collect the funding longs pay. Every action — USDC class transfers, GTC limit orders, cancels — is an ABI-encoded raw action to the CoreWriter precompile, bundled through the merkle-verified BoringVault manager in one transaction. I designed the sizing, allocation and close rules; the PT-discount variant (Pendle PT long + fixed perp short to maturity) is the same book with a fixed-yield leg.

sections.heading: Sizing and allocation
sections.body_md:
```
C = 0.995 · total_usdc            x · (1 + 1/lev) ≤ C   ->  x ≈ 0.75·C spot, 0.25·C margin at 3x
alloc_i = budget · f_i / Σ f      (funding-weighted within tier; f_i ≤ 0 dropped; < $10 dropped)
q = floor(alloc_i / (px·(1+0.005)), szDecimals)     perp_qty = spot_qty
margin_i = q · px / lev ;  requirements × 1.005 buffer
```
USDC is routed EVM → perp → spot in that order with final-state assertions; no open or close is attempted while any order rests.

sections.heading: Risk rules
sections.body_md:
| trigger | threshold | action | cadence |
|---|---|---|---|
| funding sign | latest hourly print ≤ 0 | close both legs | hourly :31 |
| liquidation proximity | px ≥ 0.8 × liquidationPx | close both legs | 15 min |
| hedge drift | abs(spot_value/perp_value − 1) > 5% | close; redeploy on next idle-capital job | 5 min |
| orphaned leg | spot > $5 with no perp, or perp with spot ≤ $5 | cancel orders, close open leg | 5 min |
| zombie orders | any resting order | cancel all | 10 min |

Short liquidation (isolated): `px_liq = entry · (1 + 1/lev) / (1 + maint)` — at 3x the liquidation price is ~31% above entry. Funding is credited to the perp account while spot gains sit on the spot ledger, so a sustained rally drains perp equity even though the book is flat; the 0.8 × liq guard is the automatic backstop — and at 3x it sits only +5.3% above entry, far inside that headroom.

**What the real data says (Hyperliquid funding + Binance/HL spot, 2026-07-25 → 10-23, candle opens, no look-ahead):** funding averaged 7–10%/yr across the four assets with 7–14% of hourly prints at or below zero, and every asset rallied 28–42% over the quarter. The gross opportunity was therefore ~7%/yr on capital at best — no rule set could have earned much.

The production rule set acts on a single hourly print, so each negative print closed a hedged book and paid ~45 bps of spot notional to reopen it (12.5 bps open + 10 bps entry slippage + 22.5 bps close, taker-side; production rested GTC limit orders, so maker economics would roughly halve this). At 3x the 0.8 × liq guard is only +5.3% from entry — not the ~31% to liquidation — so it also fired through the rally. Result: 409 closes, $35.1k of costs on closed round-trips against $1.2k of funding on those same round-trips, -33.66% on $100k. Print-level hysteresis plus the 0.92 guard: 244 closes, -18.61%. A 24-hour-mean funding gate: 21 closes, $2.1k of costs against $1.3k funding on closed legs ($1.7k including open-leg accrual), -0.50%. The same gate at 2x: 17 closes, -0.77%. No funding gate at all, guard 0.99 only: 4 closes, +1.30% — the best row.

At 3x the result is monotone in round-trip count (the 2x row earns less per round-trip because the book is smaller, so it is not on the same curve): every close cost ~45 bps that ~9%/yr funding needs ~18 days to earn back. In this window the funding gate added nothing; the production figure moves with the part-fill seed (-33.7% to -28.5% across seeds; -30.1% with part-fills off) and the committed seed is at the pessimistic end. the rule as shipped was unviable because of its own churn, and the fix is to trade less. This is a 90-day rally regime with one cost model and one or two sizing points, so it is a postmortem of a production rule, not an alpha result. The open question it leaves is whether the live vault's P&L shows the same churn — if it does not, the cost model (taker + slippage on a limit-order system) is the thing to fix.

sections.heading: Reproduce
sections.body_md:
```
python -m strategies.dn_cluster.fetch_data     # optional: pulls HL funding + Binance 1h spot into data/
python -m strategies.dn_cluster.backtest
```
`strategy.py` = sizing, allocation, liquidation and close rules; `backtest.py` = hourly engine + PT variant; results.json renders this page.
